speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when the feeding difficulties and abdominal distension first started? Also, has your son been passing stool regularly, or is there any history of constipation or vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has your son passed any stool or gas since birth, or has there been any vomiting, particularly if it appears green or bile-stained? I also need to know if he has had any episodes of bloody or mucus-filled stools.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby ever passed a normal stool, or have there been any delays in the first bowel movement after birth? I also need to know if there is any family history of Hirschsprung disease or thyroid issues.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray. I also need to know if the baby has ever had a rectal exam or an enema performed that resulted in a significant release of gas or stool.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-ray shows dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction. A subsequent Barium Enema revealed a transition zone in the distal colon, which is compatible with Hirschsprung disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging findings strongly support a diagnosis of Hirschsprung disease. I will now confirm this with a definitive test. REQUEST TEST: Rectal_Biopsy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Rectal Biopsy confirms the diagnosis of Hirschsprung disease by showing an absence of ganglion cells in the myenteric and submucosal plexuses, along with hypertrophied nerve trunks.
